title: Gan Ying's mission toward Daqin
summary: In 97 CE the Han Protector General Ban Chao sent his subordinate Gan Ying toward Daqin, the Roman Empire. Gan Ying crossed Parthia (Anxi) and reached Tiaozhi beside a great sea, read by the translator as Characene at the head of the Persian Gulf. Parthian sailors described the voyage as long and dangerous, and he gave up the crossing. His exact route, and the identity of Tiaozhi, are debated.

uncertainty.note: Hou Hanshu (Hill translation): "In the ninth year [97 CE]" Ban Chao sent Gan Ying; the chapter introduction also gives 97 CE for his journey to the Western Sea. Yang (2014) gives "AD 97".

as_recorded.calendar: Han regnal year, translator's CE gloss
as_recorded.value: In the ninth yongyuan year [97 CE], during the reign of Emperor He, the Protector General Ban Chao sent Gan Ying to Da Qin

where.modern_name: Head of the Persian Gulf (Charax Spasinu, Characene, Iraq), as Hill identifies Tiaozhi; Yang favours Antioch on the Orontes, Syria
where.historical_name: Tiaozhi (Characene and Susiana) under Anxi (Parthia); Gan Ying set out from Han Protectorate territory in the Tarim Basin region

waypoints.date: 97 CE (start; Hill: presumably from somewhere in the Tarim Basin)
waypoints.label: Tarim Basin, the likely starting region of Ban Chao's envoy according to Hill's appendix; the exact starting point is not stated.
Tiaozhi (Characene and Susiana) next to a large sea, the Persian Gulf in Hill's reading; Yang prefers Antioch in Syria. The road across Anxi is disputed.

importance.justification: The furthest recorded Han journey toward the Roman world, one of the early contacts between the two empires.

reviewer_note: Least sure of the destination: Hill reads Tiaozhi as Characene at the head of the Persian Gulf, while Yang favours Antioch on the Orontes in Syria, so confidence is contested and the 600 km uncertainty does not cover the Syrian reading. The Tarim Basin start is Hill's presumption, not a stated place; the road across Parthia is not mapped because Hill says it is uncertain.

beats.caption: Ban Chao sends Gan Ying west from the Tarim Basin region toward Daqin; he crosses Parthian territory by a route that is debated.
He reaches Tiaozhi beside a large sea, where Parthian sailors describe the crossing as very long and hard.
Hearing this, Gan Ying gives up his plan to cross; his journey had still gathered information on the Roman Empire.
